messages:
ali: hit a confusing UX while onboarding — Go generator sample app keeps streaming after the client aborts. simplest repro attached. feels like SDK retry/auth paths are using Context.Background() and resuscitating streams even after request ctx cancel.

ali: repro snippet:
```go
iter := sdk.Generator("compact").Stream(r.Context(), Prompt{Text: "outline"})
for iter.Next() {
  if _, err := w.Write([]byte(iter.Text())); err != nil {
    log.Println("write error", err)
    return
  }
}
```

mira: i've seen this. two things to fix: (1) thread parent ctx into any background refresh/reconnect so it respects cancel, (2) expose an explicit Close(ctx) on the iterator so handler code can tear it down without cancelling whole req ctx.

owen: agree. Close(ctx) semantics: idempotent, unblocks Next(), Err() returns ErrCanceled or ErrClosed. Close should attempt graceful shutdown then force-close transport if the provided ctx expires.

ali: +1. i'll sketch API and add a README cookbook showing HTTP handler pattern: on write error call iter.Close(ctxWithTimeout) then return. avoids leaking goroutines.

mira: also audit sampleapps for Context.Background() in auth/refresh code. those examples teach bad defaults. maybe a docs note: "Do not use context.Background() for long-lived network operations inside SDK internals; accept a parent ctx instead."

owen: unit tests: 1) net.Pipe fake server that keeps sending; call Close and assert Next returns within 50ms. 2) auth refresh race: force token refresh mid-stream and ensure Close cancels reconnect.

infra-bot: action: open draft PR with API + tests, tag infra/eng-ml for review.

ali: filing PR now, will include sampleapp updates and README snippet. thanks! :thumbsup:
